newsitem.title: UK: Lloyd's starts broker regulation discussion.
newsitem.headline: Lloyd's starts broker regulation discussion.

text.p: Lloyd's of London on Monday began a discussion over regulation of its brokers by issuing proposals on how to change its ways of supervising the insurance market's intermediaries.
Lloyd's has come up with a number of potential innovations such as drawing up core principles and a code of conduct for all brokers as well as the registration of key directors and senior employees.
The insurance market also proposes to distinguish brokers on the basis of size, nature of business and the quality of management.
The publication of the discussion document follows a recommendation last month that Lloyd's supervision be handed over to an external authority.

That recommendation was made by a working group, which was set up last year in the wake of the 'Reconstruction and Renewal' rescue package that saved the market from collapse from huge losses run up between 1988 and 1992.
